title: Number rows without grouping them
summary: A window function calculates across related rows while keeping each row visible.
introduction: A window function calculates across related rows while keeping each row visible. Your task: Reverse the window ordering and predict the numbers.
learningObjectives: Reverse the window ordering and predict the numbers.
Explain the example for number rows without grouping them

blocks.text: A window function calculates across related rows while keeping each row visible. row_number can number a sorted result.
Use PostgreSQL in a new practice database through psql or a database editor. These are PostgreSQL examples, not SQLite. They do not run in this site's SQL playground. Use only sample data.

blocks.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES ('Moon Trip',60),('Tiny Seed',20))
SELECT title,row_number() OVER (ORDER BY pages,title) AS reading_order FROM books ORDER BY reading_order;
blocks.title: Number rows without grouping them

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`row_number` numbers rows according to its window order while keeping those rows separate.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Tiny Seed gets 1 and Moon Trip gets 2.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A window ORDER BY sets the calculation order. Use an outer ORDER BY when the displayed row order matters too.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Reverse the window ordering and predict the numbers.
